title: Hayden Panettiere’s 911 Call: Brother Brian Hickerson’s Desperate Plea to Save Actress’s Life【Page Six】
body:
The world was stunned on August 16 when actress Hayden Panettiere, best known for her breakout role on “Heroes” and a string of high‑profile film and television projects, was found dead at the age of 36. A newly released 911 audio dispatch, obtained by CBS News, has now shed light on the frantic moments that preceded her death, revealing that her brother‑in‑law, Zach Hickerson, made desperate attempts to revive her while emergency responders raced to the scene. The harrowing call, which captured Hickerson’s pleas and the frantic instructions from dispatchers, has added a painful new layer to the tragedy that has already rippled through the entertainment community and her legion of fans.

The 911 recording begins with a shaky voice identifying the caller as “Zach Hickerson,” a close family member who discovered Panettiere unresponsive in her Los Angeles home. He immediately reports that she is not breathing and that there is no pulse. Dispatchers, adhering to protocol, instruct him to begin CPR, asking him to “push hard and fast in the center of the chest.” Hickerson’s voice trembles as he attempts to follow the guidance, repeatedly asking whether he is doing it correctly. The call captures the raw, unfiltered panic of a loved one thrust into a life‑or‑death situation, underscoring the often‑overlooked reality that even those closest to celebrities are vulnerable to the same medical emergencies that affect anyone.

The audio also reveals the rapid escalation of the emergency response. Within minutes, paramedics are on the way, and the dispatcher urges Hickerson to keep performing chest compressions while they await arrival. The conversation shifts from frantic instructions to a stark, clinical tone as the paramedics arrive, confirming that they have begun advanced life‑support measures. Despite their efforts, the dispatch notes a “no return of spontaneous circulation,” indicating that resuscitation attempts were unsuccessful. The call ends with a somber acknowledgment that Panettiere had passed, leaving Hickerson in a state of shock and grief.

Industry insiders and fans have responded to the newly released footage with a mixture of sorrow and a renewed call for awareness about cardiac emergencies. While details about the exact cause of Panettiere’s death have not been publicly disclosed, the incident has reignited conversations about the importance of immediate CPR training and the availability of automated external defibrillators (AEDs) in private residences. Medical experts note that bystanders who are trained and confident in performing CPR can dramatically increase survival rates, especially in cases of sudden cardiac arrest. The tragic outcome in this instance, despite Hickerson’s earnest attempts, highlights the narrow window of opportunity that emergency responders have and the critical role of rapid, effective intervention.

Panettiere’s career, which spanned from child roles in “Remember the Titans” to her iconic turn as Claire Bennet on “Heroes,” earned her a place in the cultural consciousness as a resilient, versatile performer. Colleagues have paid tribute, recalling her professionalism, warmth, and dedication to charitable causes, particularly those focused on children’s health. Her untimely death has prompted a wave of memorials across social media, with fellow actors, directors, and fans sharing personal anecdotes that paint a portrait of a generous spirit whose impact extended beyond the screen.

As the entertainment industry mourns the loss of a beloved figure, the release of the 911 call serves as a stark reminder of the fragility of life, regardless of fame or fortune. It also underscores a broader societal issue: the need for widespread emergency preparedness training and access to life‑saving equipment in private homes. In the weeks ahead, it is likely that advocacy groups will leverage Panettiere’s story to push for legislative measures that promote CPR education and AED placement, hoping to turn a personal tragedy into a catalyst for public health improvements. The hope remains that, through heightened awareness and preparedness, future emergencies may be met with the swift, effective response that can mean the difference between life and death.
